exercises.english: In 1987 the company moved its headquarters to Stuttgart.
exercises.german: 1987 verlegte das Unternehmen seinen Hauptsitz nach Stuttgart.
exercises.why: A neutral factual report takes the Präteritum verlegte, not the Perfekt.

exercises.english: The old town hall was torn down after the war.
exercises.german: Nach dem Krieg riss man das alte Rathaus ab.
exercises.why: Passive narrative with the Präteritum of the modal man.

exercises.english: My grandfather worked as a railway engineer for forty years.
exercises.german: Mein Großvater arbeitete vierzig Jahre lang als Eisenbahningenieur.
exercises.why: A biographical stretch of life is narrated in the Präteritum.

exercises.english: The committee rejected the proposal without a long discussion.
exercises.german: Der Ausschuss lehnte den Antrag ab, ohne lange zu diskutieren.
exercises.why: Präteritum lehnte ab with the zu-infinitive clause placed at the end.

exercises.english: She took over the workshop from her uncle in 2003.
exercises.german: 2003 übernahm sie die Werkstatt von ihrem Onkel.
exercises.why: Verbs of transfer and change of ownership take the Präteritum here.

exercises.english: The delegation arrived two days late.
exercises.german: Die Delegation kam zwei Tage zu spät.
exercises.why: A short factual statement in a report is built on the Präteritum kam.

exercises.english: Nobody understood the real reason for his resignation.
exercises.german: Niemand verstand den wahren Grund für seinen Rücktritt.
exercises.why: A second past event on the same narrative level stays in the Präteritum.

exercises.english: They planted apple trees all along the avenue.
exercises.german: Sie pflanzten die ganze Allee mit Apfelbäumen.
exercises.why: Präteritum pflanzten with a dative object complement mit.

exercises.english: The factory employed four hundred people in its best years.
exercises.german: Die Fabrik beschäftigte in ihren besten Jahren vierhundert Menschen.
exercises.why: A written description of a past state uses the Präteritum beschäftigte.

exercises.english: He wrote in his diary that the situation was getting worse.
exercises.german: Er schrieb in sein Tagebuch, dass die Lage schlimmer wurde.
exercises.why: The dass-clause reports a fact rather than a speaker opinion, so it stays indicative.

exercises.english: The river flooded the lower streets several times in that decade.
exercises.german: Der Fluss überflutete in jenem Jahrzehnt mehrmals die unteren Straßen.
exercises.why: Historical narration with the Präteritum of a strong verb, überflutete.

exercises.english: The minister denied having been informed about the failure.
exercises.german: Der Minister bestritt, ihn von dem Vorfall informiert zu haben.
exercises.why: Präteritum bestritt with an infinitive clause and a perfect participle inside.

exercises.english: After the lecture we walked home through the old town.
exercises.german: Nach der Vorlesung gingen wir durch die Altstadt nach Hause.
exercises.why: After a temporal preposition the narrative verb is the Präteritum gingen.

exercises.english: The publisher rejected the manuscript without reading it.
exercises.german: Der Verlag lehnte das Manuskript ab, ohne es zu lesen.
exercises.why: The pronoun es inside the infinitive clause refers back to das Manuskript.

exercises.english: Her life changed completely when she moved abroad.
exercises.german: Ihr Leben änderte sich grundlegend, als sie ins Ausland zog.
exercises.why: After als the event that sets the change in motion also takes the Präteritum zog.

exercises.english: The museum opened a new wing in the spring of that year.
exercises.german: Das Museum eröffnete im Frühjahr jenes Jahres einen neuen Flügel.
exercises.why: A dated official statement is normally written in the Präteritum.

exercises.english: He knew everybody in the village but spoke to very few.
exercises.german: Er kannte im Dorf jeden, sprach aber mit sehr wenigen.
exercises.why: Two coordinated Präteritum verbs joined by aber describe the same stretch of time.

exercises.english: The engine stopped twice on the way to the coast.
exercises.german: Der Motor blieb zweimal auf dem Weg zur Küste stehen.
exercises.why: The separable verb bleibt stehen keeps its prefix in the infinitive after bleiben.

exercises.english: They voted on the proposal only once, in November.
exercises.german: Sie stimmten nur einmal über den Antrag ab, im November.
exercises.why: The separable verb abstimmen splits as ab in the Präteritum: stimmten ab.

exercises.english: The war changed the whole region for good.
exercises.german: Der Krieg veränderte die gesamte Region für immer.
exercises.why: A general statement about the past is made in the Präteritum.

exercises.english: I had already paid the bill when she arrived.
exercises.german: Ich hatte die Rechnung schon bezahlt, als sie ankam.
exercises.why: The earlier action is Plusquamperfekt, the later one the Präteritum ankam.

exercises.english: We had never seen such heavy snowfall before that winter.
exercises.german: Vor diesem Winter hatten wir noch nie so starken Schneefall erlebt.
exercises.why: Bis with a time point turns hatte erlebt into a Plusquamperfekt.

exercises.english: The museum had closed an hour before we arrived.
exercises.german: Das Museum hatte schon eine Stunde vor unserer Ankunft geschlossen.
exercises.why: The duration vor unserer Ankunft fixes the closing as the earlier event.

exercises.english: She had studied chemistry for four years before she changed her mind.
exercises.german: Sie hatte vier Jahre Chemie studiert, bevor sie ihre Meinung änderte.
exercises.why: The length of study lies before the decision, so it is a Plusquamperfekt.

exercises.english: The letter had been lying unopened on the shelf for days.
exercises.german: Der Brief hatte tagelang ungelesen auf dem Regal gelegen.
exercises.why: A state that lasted up to a past moment is expressed with hatte gelegen.

exercises.english: He had forgotten her name, so he waited outside.
exercises.german: Er hatte ihren Namen vergessen, deshalb wartete er draußen.
exercises.why: The forgetting is the earlier event; the waiting is the Präteritum main clause.

exercises.english: By 2010 the town had grown by nearly a third.
exercises.german: Bis 2010 war die Stadt um fast ein Drittel gewachsen.
exercises.why: Bis plus a change-of-state verb takes war as the auxiliary of the Plusquamperfekt.

exercises.english: They had eaten before the film started, so they were hungry again.
exercises.german: Sie hatten vor dem Film gegessen und bekamen später wieder Hunger.
exercises.why: A hatte-gegessen clause and a Präteritum clause carry the two different time planes.

exercises.english: The teacher asked why we had not done the exercise.
exercises.german: Die Lehrerin fragte, warum wir die Übung nicht gemacht hatten.
exercises.why: The indirect question is a verb-final clause with the Plusquamperfekt at its end.

exercises.english: Once the old tree had been cut down, the view was much better.
exercises.german: Sobald der alte Baum gefällt worden war, war der Blick viel besser.
exercises.why: The Vorgangspassiv in the Plusquamperfekt is worden plus participle plus war.

exercises.english: Until that evening I had never tasted a better soup.
exercises.german: Bis zu jenem Abend hatte ich noch nie eine bessere Suppe gekostet.
exercises.why: Bis zu with a time limit marks the tasting as lying before a past moment.

exercises.english: She noticed that he had already read the message.
exercises.german: Sie merkte, dass er die Nachricht schon gelesen hatte.
exercises.why: The dass-clause reports a completed earlier event, so gelesen hatte is Plusquamperfekt.

exercises.english: The delegation had waited two hours before they were admitted.
exercises.german: Die Delegation hatte zwei Stunden gewartet, bevor sie hereingelassen wurde.
exercises.why: The waiting precedes the later passive event, so it is a Plusquamperfekt.

exercises.english: Nothing had changed in the village during all those years.
exercises.german: In all den Jahren hatte sich im Dorf nichts geändert.
exercises.why: Reflexive sich with hatte marks the state that held before the point narrated.

exercises.english: When we reached the airport, the airline had already cancelled our flight.
exercises.german: Als wir am Flughafen ankamen, hatte die Airline unseren Flug schon annulliert.
exercises.why: The main clause is Präteritum ankam, the subordinate clause Plusquamperfekt annulliert.

exercises.english: He had written three drafts before he showed anyone the text.
exercises.german: Er hatte drei Fassungen geschrieben, bevor er jemandem den Text zeigte.
exercises.why: The number of earlier attempts is expressed in the Plusquamperfekt.

exercises.english: The building had stood empty for years before the renovation began.
exercises.german: Das Gebäude hatte jahrelang leer gestanden, bevor mit dem Umbau begonnen wurde.
exercises.why: A long state that ended before a past event is a Plusquamperfekt with hatte.

exercises.english: She had trained as a nurse for six years before she switched to law.
exercises.german: Sie hatte sechs Jahre Krankenpflege gelernt, bevor sie auf Jura wechselte.
exercises.why: The training is the earlier period, expressed with hatte gelernt.

exercises.english: Both parents had worked abroad when the children were small.
exercises.german: Beide Eltern hatten im Ausland gearbeitet, als die Kinder klein waren.
exercises.why: A relative clause in the Plusquamperfekt attached to a Präteritum when-clause.

exercises.english: He had warned me twice before I understood the danger.
exercises.german: Er hatte mich zweimal gewarnt, bevor ich die Gefahr verstand.
exercises.why: The repeated earlier act takes the Plusquamperfekt, das understanding the Präteritum.

exercises.english: We had to wait at customs for three hours.
exercises.german: Wir hatten beim Zoll drei Stunden lang warten müssen.
exercises.why: In the Plusquamperfekt the modal loses its infinitive and keeps the lexical verb.

exercises.english: She was not allowed to use the service entrance.
exercises.german: Sie hatte den Personaleingang nicht benutzen dürfen.
exercises.why: A modal prohibition earlier than a past moment is hatte plus gedurft.

exercises.english: He had not been able to finish the translation in time.
exercises.german: Er hatte die Übersetzung nicht rechtzeitig fertig machen können.
exercises.why: The lexical infinitive fertig machen stays, the modal contributes gekonnt.

exercises.english: The doctor had to operate without any help.
exercises.german: Der Arzt hatte ohne jede Hilfe operieren müssen.
exercises.why: A single lexical infinitive plus a modal participle closes the clause.

exercises.english: We had to use the stairs because the lift was out of order.
exercises.german: Wir hatten die Treppe benutzen müssen, weil der Aufzug außer Betrieb war.
exercises.why: The modal in the Plusquamperfekt takes gemusst, the reason clause uses the Präteritum.

exercises.english: Nobody was permitted to park in the courtyard.
exercises.german: Niemand hatte im Innenhof parken dürfen.
exercises.why: A separable prefix stays whole in the final position: parken dürfen.

exercises.english: She had to give up smoking after the second operation.
exercises.german: Sie hatte nach der zweiten Operation mit dem Rauchen aufhören müssen.
exercises.why: The mit-infinitive and the modal participle form the clause-final verb cluster.

exercises.english: The school was supposed to close at five, and we had to wait outside.
exercises.german: Die Schule hatte um fünf schließen sollen, und wir hatten bis sechs draußen warten müssen.
exercises.why: Two modal Plusquamperfekte: hatte schließen sollen and hatten warten müssen.

exercises.english: I had to look up three words in the dictionary.
exercises.german: Ich hatte drei Wörter im Wörterbuch nachschlagen müssen.
exercises.why: The separable prefix of nachschlagen reappears in the infinitive at the end.

exercises.english: They were not supposed to discuss the case with the press.
exercises.german: Sie hatten mit der Presse nicht über den Fall sprechen dürfen.
exercises.why: Negation sits between the prepositional phrase and the infinitive cluster.

exercises.english: We had to book a second hotel because the first was full.
exercises.german: Wir hatten ein zweites Hotel buchen müssen, weil das erste voll war.
exercises.why: The modal in the second past governs the lexical infinitive at the clause end.

exercises.english: He had been unable to reach her on the phone.
exercises.german: Er hatte sie telefonisch nicht erreichen können.
exercises.why: A negated modal ability earlier than a past point is hatte plus gekonnt.

exercises.english: Nobody had been allowed to use the old bridge any more.
exercises.german: Niemand hatte die alte Brücke noch benutzen dürfen.
exercises.why: The temporal adverb noch and the modal gedurft mark the earlier restriction.

exercises.english: We had to take a taxi because the last bus had already left the square.
exercises.german: Wir hatten ein Taxi nehmen müssen, weil der letzte Bus schon gegangen war.
exercises.why: A modal Plusquamperfekt in the main clause with a war-clause as the reason.

exercises.english: I had to work overtime for three weeks that autumn.
exercises.german: Ich hatte in jenem Herbst drei Wochen lang Überstunden machen müssen.
exercises.why: A lexical infinitive with zu plus the modal participle gemusst closes the clause.

exercises.english: They had to cancel the wedding because of the storm.
exercises.german: Sie hatten die Hochzeit wegen des Sturms absagen müssen.
exercises.why: A separable verb stays intact in the infinitive before the modal participle.

exercises.english: We were not supposed to mention the name of the client.
exercises.german: Wir hatten den Namen des Kunden nicht nennen dürfen.
exercises.why: The modal Plusquamperfekt places nicht in front of the lexical infinitive.

exercises.english: He had wanted to study medicine, but he changed his mind.
exercises.german: Er hatte Medizin studieren wollen, entschied sich dann aber anders.
exercises.why: The earlier intention is a modal Plusquamperfekt with gewollt.

exercises.english: The tenant had to pay for the new window himself.
exercises.german: Der Mieter hatte das neue Fenster selbst bezahlen müssen.
exercises.why: The reflexive-looking selbst is an adverb placed before the final verb cluster.

exercises.english: We had to leave the ship before it reached the harbour.
exercises.german: Wir hatten das Schiff verlassen müssen, bevor es den Hafen erreichte.
exercises.why: The modal Plusquamperfekt precedes a bevor-clause in the Präteritum.

exercises.skill: Two past events in one sentence
exercises.english: After we had paid, the waiter brought the bill again.
exercises.german: Nachdem wir bezahlt hatten, brachte der Kellner die Rechnung noch einmal.
exercises.why: A nachdem-clause in the Plusquamperfekt precedes the Präteritum main clause.

exercises.skill: Two past events in one sentence
exercises.english: Because he had lost his passport, he could not board the plane.
exercises.german: Weil er seinen Pass verloren hatte, konnte er nicht in das Flugzeug einsteigen.
exercises.why: The reason sits in a Plusquamperfekt, the consequence in the Präteritum.

exercises.skill: Two past events in one sentence
exercises.english: She had already locked the door when the phone rang.
exercises.german: Sie hatte die Tür schon abgeschlossen, als das Telefon klingelte.
exercises.why: The completed action before the als-clause is a Plusquamperfekt.

exercises.skill: Two past events in one sentence
exercises.english: When I arrived, the film had already started.
exercises.german: Als ich ankam, hatte der Film schon angefangen.
exercises.why: A Präteritum als-clause is followed by the Plusquamperfekt for the earlier event.

exercises.skill: Two past events in one sentence
exercises.english: The office had closed at six, so nobody answered the phone.
exercises.german: Das Büro hatte um sechs geschlossen, deshalb ging niemand ans Telefon.
exercises.why: The earlier closing uses hatte, the later reaction the Präteritum ging.

exercises.skill: Two past events in one sentence
exercises.english: After they had waited an hour, they finally got a taxi.
exercises.german: Nachdem sie eine Stunde lang gewartet hatten, bekamen sie endlich ein Taxi.
exercises.why: The duration of waiting belongs to the Plusquamperfekt, the outcome to the Präteritum.

exercises.skill: Two past events in one sentence
exercises.english: She did not go on holiday because she had not saved enough money.
exercises.german: Sie fuhr nicht in den Urlaub, weil sie nicht genug Geld gespart hatte.
exercises.why: A negated Präteritum main clause with a Plusquamperfekt reason clause.

exercises.skill: Two past events in one sentence
exercises.english: The meeting began only after everyone had arrived.
exercises.german: Die Besprechung begann erst, nachdem alle angekommen waren.
exercises.why: The temporal subordinate clause closes the sentence with the auxiliary war.

exercises.skill: Two past events in one sentence
exercises.english: When the storm had passed, they left the campsite.
exercises.german: Als der Sturm vorübergezogen war, verließen sie den Campingplatz.
exercises.why: The earlier event is war plus participle, the main clause is the Präteritum verließen.

exercises.skill: Two past events in one sentence
exercises.english: He was late because he had missed the earlier train.
exercises.german: Er kam zu spät, weil er den früheren Zug verpasst hatte.
exercises.why: Two different time planes on two sides of the weil-clause.

exercises.skill: Two past events in one sentence
exercises.english: After the letter had arrived, she called the office.
exercises.german: Nachdem der Brief angekommen war, erkundigte sie sich bei der Firma.
exercises.why: An intransitive verb of movement takes war in the Plusquamperfekt.

exercises.skill: Two past events in one sentence
exercises.english: They ate well because they had bought groceries on the way.
exercises.german: Sie aßen gut, weil sie unterwegs Lebensmittel eingekauft hatten.
exercises.why: The Präteritum aßen and the Plusquamperfekt gekauft hatten cover different layers.

exercises.skill: Two past events in one sentence
exercises.english: The shop reopened only after it had been renovated.
exercises.german: Der Laden öffnete erst wieder, nachdem er renoviert worden war.
exercises.why: A passive Plusquamperfekt closes the nachdem-clause.

exercises.skill: Two past events in one sentence
exercises.english: I understood the question only after I had read the text twice.
exercises.german: Ich verstand die Frage erst, nachdem ich den Text zweimal gelesen hatte.
exercises.why: Erst marks the later event, the nachdem-clause the earlier one.

exercises.skill: Two past events in one sentence
exercises.english: Because they had not reserved a table, they had to wait.
exercises.german: Weil sie keinen Tisch reserviert hatten, mussten sie warten.
exercises.why: A Plusquamperfekt reason clause followed by a modal Präteritum.

exercises.skill: Two past events in one sentence
exercises.english: When she had finished her report, everyone left the room.
exercises.german: Als sie ihren Bericht beendet hatte, verließen alle den Raum.
exercises.why: The two time planes are marked by hatte beendet and Präteritum verließen.

exercises.skill: Two past events in one sentence
exercises.english: The address was wrong because he had copied it carelessly.
exercises.german: Die Adresse war falsch, weil er sie fahrlässig abgeschrieben hatte.
exercises.why: The state war falsch belongs to a past moment, the cause is earlier still.

exercises.skill: Two past events in one sentence
exercises.english: The concert began before we had found our seats.
exercises.german: Das Konzert begann, bevor wir unsere Plätze gefunden hatten.
exercises.why: The later event first in the main clause, the earlier one in the bevor-clause.

exercises.skill: Two past events in one sentence
exercises.english: After the war had ended, thousands of families returned home.
exercises.german: Nachdem der Krieg geendet hatte, kehrten tausend Familien nach Hause zurück.
exercises.why: A Plusquamperfekt nachdem-clause and a Präteritum main clause with a separable prefix.

exercises.skill: Two past events in one sentence
exercises.english: She could not enter because she had left her pass at home.
exercises.german: Sie konnte nicht eintreten, weil sie ihren Ausweis zu Hause gelassen hatte.
exercises.why: A modal Präteritum in the main clause and a Plusquamperfekt in the weil-clause.

exercises.skill: Choosing Präteritum vs. Perfekt in writing
exercises.english: Write a formal report sentence: the council met in March and decided to close the pool.
exercises.german: Der Stadtrat trat im März zusammen und beschloss, das Freibad zu schließen.
exercises.why: A formal report takes the Präteritum for both the meeting and the decision.

exercises.skill: Choosing Präteritum vs. Perfekt in writing
exercises.english: Say casually at the office that you have already sent the file.
exercises.german: Ich habe die Datei schon geschickt.
exercises.why: Spoken German about a current result uses the Perfekt.

exercises.skill: Choosing Präteritum vs. Perfekt in writing
exercises.english: Give the plot of the film: the hero leaves the island and never returns.
exercises.german: Der Held verlässt die Insel und kehrt nie zurück.
exercises.why: Plot summaries are narrated in the Präteritum regardless of the film is recent.

exercises.skill: Choosing Präteritum vs. Perfekt in writing
exercises.english: Explain to a friend that you have visited the new exhibition three times.
exercises.german: Ich habe die neue Ausstellung dreimal besucht.
exercises.why: An experience up to today belongs in the Perfekt.

exercises.skill: Choosing Präteritum vs. Perfekt in writing
exercises.english: In a history lesson: the economy collapsed in 1929 and unemployment rose sharply.
exercises.german: Die Wirtschaft brach 1929 zusammen, und die Arbeitslosigkeit stieg stark.
exercises.why: A history lesson is written narrative, so the Präteritum dominates.

exercises.skill: Choosing Präteritum vs. Perfekt in writing
exercises.english: Tell your flatmate that you have already eaten.
exercises.german: Ich habe schon gegessen.
exercises.why: The state still holds now, so the Perfekt is the natural choice in speech.

exercises.skill: Choosing Präteritum vs. Perfekt in writing
exercises.english: In an official report: two employees left the company in 2020 without notice.
exercises.german: Zwei Mitarbeiter verließen das Unternehmen 2020 ohne Kündigungsfrist.
exercises.why: Official reports look backwards and take the Präteritum verließen.

exercises.skill: Choosing Präteritum vs. Perfekt in writing
exercises.english: Say that you have already paid the invoice.
exercises.german: Ich habe die Rechnung schon bezahlt.
exercises.why: A completed action with present relevance is a Perfekt, not a Plusquamperfekt.

exercises.skill: Choosing Präteritum vs. Perfekt in writing
exercises.english: Summarise the legend: the treasure was buried in 1840 and nobody found it again.
exercises.german: Der Schatz wurde 1840 vergraben und nie wieder gefunden.
exercises.why: A narrative summary prefers the Präteritum of the passive, wurde vergraben.

exercises.skill: Choosing Präteritum vs. Perfekt in writing
exercises.english: Mention casually that you have met her a few times.
exercises.german: Ich habe sie ein paarmal getroffen.
exercises.why: An informal mention of a past meeting uses the Perfekt getroffen.

exercises.skill: Choosing Präteritum vs. Perfekt in writing
exercises.english: In a company history: the founder established the workshop in 1902 and ran it until 1934.
exercises.german: Der Gründer richtete 1902 die Werkstatt ein und führte sie bis 1934.
exercises.why: Company histories are continuous narration and use the Präteritum throughout.

exercises.skill: Choosing Präteritum vs. Perfekt in writing
exercises.english: Say that you have lost your keys again.
exercises.german: Ich habe schon wieder meinen Schlüssel verloren.
exercises.why: A complaint about the present uses the Perfekt with a separable-free participle.

exercises.skill: Choosing Präteritum vs. Perfekt in writing
exercises.english: In a news report: the storm damaged three houses in the village centre.
exercises.german: Der Sturm beschädigte drei Häuser im Zentrum des Dorfes.
exercises.why: A printed news report narrates the event in the Präteritum.

exercises.skill: Choosing Präteritum vs. Perfekt in writing
exercises.english: Tell someone that you have already read the whole report.
exercises.german: Ich habe den ganzen Bericht schon gelesen.
exercises.why: The result is relevant now, so the Perfekt is correct in speech.

exercises.skill: Choosing Präteritum vs. Perfekt in writing
exercises.english: In a review: the film was long, slow and nevertheless impressive.
exercises.german: Der Film war lang, langsam und trotzdem eindrucksvoll.
exercises.why: A critical judgement about a past film is expressed with the Präteritum war.

exercises.skill: Choosing Präteritum vs. Perfekt in writing
exercises.english: Say casually that you have never been to a football match.
exercises.german: Ich bin noch nie bei einem Fußballspiel gewesen.
exercises.why: A negated experience uses the Perfekt of sein with the participle gewesen.

exercises.skill: Choosing Präteritum vs. Perfekt in writing
exercises.english: In minutes: the committee rejected the amendment on Tuesday evening.
exercises.german: Der Ausschuss wies am Dienstagabend den Änderungsantrag zurück.
exercises.why: Minutes record a past decision and take the Präteritum wies zurück.

exercises.skill: Choosing Präteritum vs. Perfekt in writing
exercises.english: Ask a colleague casually whether he has finished the report.
exercises.german: Hast du den Bericht schon fertig?
exercises.why: A question about a state that holds now invites the Perfekt, not the Präteritum.

exercises.skill: Choosing Präteritum vs. Perfekt in writing
